023/**
024 * Describes a key (or several fallback keys) resolved against a {@link LogProperties}
025 * instance - start with {@link LogProperties#forKey(String)} - and also serves as the
026 * namespace for the shared property machinery: {@link Result}, {@link Validator}, and the
027 * property-specific exceptions.
028 *
029 * @see LogProperties
030 */
031@CaseChanging
032public interface LogProperty {
033
034        /**
035         * The first key tried.
036         * @return key.
037         */
038        public String key();
039
040        /**
041         * Every key tried, in order - the first key given to
042         * {@link LogProperties#forKey(String)}/{@link LogProperties#forKey(String, String)}
043         * followed by any added via {@link #or(String)}/{@link #or(String, String)}.
044         * @return keys.
045         */
046        public List<String> keys();
047
048        /**
049         * The properties this key (or keys) will be looked up against.
050         * @return properties.
051         */
052        public LogProperties properties();
053
054        /**
055         * Resolves the property as a raw string.
056         * @return result.
057         */
058        public Result<String> ofString();
059
060        /**
061         * Resolves the property as a list, using {@link LogProperties#listOrNull(String)}.
062         * @return result.
063         */
064        public Result<List<String>> ofList();
065
066        /**
067         * Resolves the property as a map, using {@link LogProperties#mapOrNull(String)}.
068         * @return result.
069         */
070        public Result<Map<String, String>> ofMap();
071
072        /**
073         * Parses a case-insensitive enum value, ignoring leading and trailing whitespace, and
074         * reports the valid property values when parsing fails. Enum names and additional
075         * values are shown in lowercase, as property values conventionally are.
076         * @param <E> enum type.
077         * @param enumType enum class.
078         * @param input input value.
079         * @param additionalValues accepted aliases or other values supported by the property.
080         * @return parsed enum value.
081         */
082        static <E extends Enum<E>> E enumValue(Class<E> enumType, String input, String... additionalValues) {
083                /*
084                 * A properties file keeps trailing whitespace, which is invisible in an editor.
085                 */
086                String value = input.strip();
087                try {
088                        return Enum.valueOf(enumType, value.toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT));
089                }
090                catch (IllegalArgumentException e) {
091                        var available = new LinkedHashSet<String>();
092                        EnumSet.allOf(enumType).stream().map(v -> v.name().toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT)).forEach(available::add);
093                        Arrays.stream(additionalValues).map(v -> v.toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT)).forEach(available::add);
094                        throw new IllegalArgumentException("'" + value + "' is not a valid value for " + enumType.getCanonicalName()
095                                        + ". Valid values: " + String.join(", ", available.stream().map(v -> "'" + v + "'").toList()), e);
096                }
097        }
098
099        /**
100         * Renders a URI for diagnostics with user information and all query values redacted.
101         * The returned text is for display, not for making requests.
102         * @param uri URI to display.
103         * @return redacted URI text.
104         */
105        static String redactUri(URI uri) {
106                return LogRedactor.redactUri(uri);
107        }
108
109        /**
110         * Resolves the property as an int.
111         * @return result.
112         */
113        default Result<Integer> ofInt() {
114                return ofString().map(v -> Integer.parseInt(v.strip()));
115        }
116
117        /**
118         * Resolves the property as a long.
119         * @return result.
120         */
121        default Result<Long> ofLong() {
122                return ofString().map(Long::parseLong);
123        }
124
125        /**
126         * Resolves the property as a boolean. Only <code>true</code> and <code>false</code>
127         * (case-insensitive) are valid; any other value is an error.
128         * @return result.
129         * @apiNote new properties should prefer a small enum with <code>true</code> and
130         * <code>false</code> as aliases, parsed from {@link #ofString()}, so the property can
131         * grow more choices later.
132         */
133        default Result<Boolean> ofBoolean() {
134                return ofString().map(LogProperty::parseBoolean);
135        }
136
137        private static Boolean parseBoolean(String input) {
138                String value = input.strip();
139                if (value.equalsIgnoreCase("true")) {
140                        return true;
141                }
142                if (value.equalsIgnoreCase("false")) {
143                        return false;
144                }
145                throw new IllegalArgumentException(
146                                "'" + value + "' is not a valid value for java.lang.Boolean. Valid values: 'true', 'false'");
147        }
148
149        /**
150         * Resolves the property as a URI.
151         * @return result.
152         */
153        default Result<URI> ofURI() {
154                return ofString().map(URI::new);
155        }
156
157        /**
158         * Resolves the property as a {@link LogProviderRef} for component provision.
159         * @return result.
160         * @see LogOutput#of(LogProviderRef)
161         */
162        default Result<LogProviderRef> ofProviderRef() {
163                return switch (ofURI()) {
164                        case Result.Success<URI> s -> mapValue(s, LogProviderRef.of(s.value(), s.key()));
165                        case Result.Missing<URI> m -> m.convert();
166                        case Result.Error<URI> e -> e.convert();
167                };
168        }
169
170        /**
171         * Resolves the property as a {@link LogProviderRef} and then maps it to a
172         * {@link LogProvider}.
173         * @param <U> provider type.
174         * @param mapper function to map to provider.
175         * @return result.
176         * @see LogOutput#of(LogProviderRef)
177         */
178        default <U> Result<LogProvider<U>> ofProvider(
179                        PropertyFunction<LogProviderRef, LogProvider<U>, ? super Exception> mapper) {
180                return ofProviderRef().map(mapper);
181        }
182
183        /**
184         * Rewraps a value that was already derived from success's value, keeping the
185         * {@link PropertySuccess}'s origin (topProperties/properties/key/rawValue/kind)
186         * intact - useful for a conversion step that cannot itself throw, so
187         * {@link Result#map(PropertyFunction)} would be overkill, but that still needs to
188         * keep the result's origin intact for a later conversion step's error message.
189         * @param <T> success's value type.
190         * @param <U> new value type.
191         * @param success success to take the origin from.
192         * @param value already-converted value to wrap.
193         * @return new success of the same shape as success, wrapping value.
194         */
195        static <T, U> Result.Success<U> mapValue(Result.Success<T> success, U value) {
196                return switch (success) {
197                        case PropertySuccess<T> ps -> new PropertySuccess<>(ps.topProperties(), ps.properties(), ps.key(),
198                                        ps.rawValue(), ps.kind(), value, ps.sensitive());
199                };
200        }
201
202        /**
203         * Builds a rich error from a failed conversion of a previously successful result -
204         * package-visible (rather than private) only so the top-level {@link PropertySuccess}
205         * can call it from {@link Result#map(PropertyFunction)}.
206         * @param <U> the converted value type.
207         * @param previousResult the success being converted.
208         * @param e the conversion failure.
209         * @return a rich error result.
210         */
211        static <U> Result.Error<U> richError(Result.Success<?> previousResult, Exception e) {
212                return richError(previousResult, e, "Error converting property");
213        }
214
215        /**
216         * Like {@link #richError(Result.Success, Exception)} but for a property whose value
217         * was used to invoke {@link LogProvider#provide(String, LogConfig)} rather than a
218         * plain same-property type conversion - see
219         * {@link #provideValue(Result, String, LogConfig)}. The provider constructs a
220         * genuinely separate component with its own property tree, so a failure inside it
221         * (typically already a complete, self-describing {@link ValidationException} of its
222         * own) must not be labeled "Error converting property": this property's own value
223         * converted just fine, it merely triggered a provider that failed on its own terms.
224         * @param <U> the provided component type.
225         * @param previousResult the success whose value was provided from.
226         * @param e the provisioning failure.
227         * @return a rich error result.
228         */
229        static <U> Result.Error<U> providingError(Result.Success<?> previousResult, Exception e) {
230                return richError(previousResult, e, "Failure providing from property");
231        }
232
233        /**
234         * Like {@link Result#map(PropertyFunction)} but specifically for the "resolve to a
235         * {@link LogProvider}, then {@link LogProvider#provide(String, LogConfig) provide}"
236         * step used by output/encoder/appender resolution. A plain {@link Result#map} would
237         * relabel any failure from {@code provide(...)} as "Error converting property" even
238         * though this property's own value converted to a provider just fine - see
239         * {@link #providingError(Result.Success, Exception)}.
240         * @param <T> component type.
241         * @param providerResult an already-resolved provider, e.g. from
242         * {@link LogProperty#ofProvider(PropertyFunction)}.
243         * @param name component name passed to
244         * {@link LogProvider#provide(String, LogConfig)}.
245         * @param config config passed to {@link LogProvider#provide(String, LogConfig)}.
246         * @return the provided component, or the same {@link Result.Missing}/
247         * {@link Result.Error} a plain conversion would have produced.
248         */
249        static <T> Result<T> provideValue(Result<LogProvider<T>> providerResult, String name, LogConfig config) {
250                return switch (providerResult) {
251                        case Result.Success<LogProvider<T>> s -> {
252                                try {
253                                        yield mapValue(s, s.value().provide(name, config));
254                                }
255                                catch (Exception e) {
256                                        yield providingError(s, e);
257                                }
258                        }
259                        case Result.Missing<LogProvider<T>> m -> m.convert();
260                        case Result.Error<LogProvider<T>> e -> e.convert();
261                };
262        }
263
264        private static <U> Result.Error<U> richError(Result.Success<?> previousResult, Exception e, String chainedLabel) {
265                String fqk = previousResult.key();
266                PropertySuccess<?> ps = switch (previousResult) {
267                        case PropertySuccess<?> p -> p;
268                };
269                if (ps.sensitive()) {
270                        // Converter messages, causes and suppressed exceptions may quote the secret.
271                        e = LogRedactor.redactException(e);
272                }
273                if (ps.kind() == PropertySuccess.Kind.VALUE) {
274                        String resolvedKey = ps.topProperties().description(fqk);
275                        String message = "Error for property. key: " + resolvedKey + ", " + e.getMessage();
276                        return new Result.Error<>(resolvedKey, message, e);
277                }
278                var badProps = ps.properties();
279                String badDescription = badProps.description(fqk);
280                String resolvedKey = "'" + fqk + "' from " + badDescription;
281                boolean chained = e instanceof PropertyConvertException || e instanceof ValidationException;
282                String own;
283                if (chained) {
284                        own = chainedLabel + ". key: " + resolvedKey + ", value: '" + ps.valueDescription() + "'";
285                }
286                else {
287                        String exceptionPrefix = e.getClass() == IllegalArgumentException.class ? "" : errorName(e) + " ";
288                        /*
289                         * A converter's message can quote the value it could not convert.
290                         */
291                        String detail = ps.sensitive() ? "the value is not shown because it is sensitive" : e.getMessage();
292                        own = "Error for property. key: " + resolvedKey + ", " + exceptionPrefix + detail;
293                }
294                /*
295                 * Only worth a "Tried:" line if topProperties actually searched more broadly than
296                 * where the value was found (a chained/composite LogProperties) - for a
297                 * non-chained property, topProperties().description(fqk) is identical to
298                 * badDescription above, so appending it would just repeat the "key: ... from X"
299                 * text already shown on this exact message with nothing new to say.
300                 */
301                String triedDescription = ps.topProperties().description(fqk);
302                if (!triedDescription.equals(badDescription)) {
303                        String tried = "Tried: '" + fqk + "' from " + triedDescription;
304                        if (tried.length() > 120) {
305                                var sources = new ArrayList<String>();
306                                ps.topProperties().visit(fqk, (source, sourceKey) -> {
307                                        sources.add(source.description(sourceKey));
308                                        return null;
309                                });
310                                tried = "Tried:\n    '" + fqk + "' from:\n        " + String.join(",\n        ", sources);
311                        }
312                        own += "\n" + tried;
313                }
314                /*
315                 * Root cause first: e's own message already has everything beneath this layer
316                 * fully rendered (its own recursive "↳" trail included, if any), so this layer's
317                 * contribution is appended as one more arrow line rather than prepended - keeps
318                 * the deepest, most specific failure at the top no matter how many layers wrap
319                 * it. A non-chained e (a plain library exception like NumberFormatException) has
320                 * nothing beneath it to defer to, so its own message stays the whole (root) text.
321                 */
322                String message = chained ? e.getMessage() + "\n  ↳ " + own.replace("\n", "\n    ") : own;
323                return new Result.Error<>(resolvedKey, message, e);
324        }
325
326        /**
327         * Prefers {@link PropertyProblem#errorName()} (a short, stable name) over the
328         * exception's actual class name - a foreign exception (not one of ours) just gets its
329         * full class name as before.
330         */
331        private static String errorName(Exception e) {
332                if (e instanceof PropertyProblem pp) {
333                        return pp.errorName();
334                }
335                return e.getClass().getName();
336        }
337
338        /**
339         * Checks that value is not null, throwing {@link PropertyMissingException} naming key
340         * if it is. Useful for a property that is required but was set programmatically (e.g.
341         * a builder setter) rather than resolved through {@link #ofString()}/etc, so there is
342         * no {@link Result} to check for missing-ness.
343         * @param <T> value type.
344         * @param key property key, used only in the exception message.
345         * @param value value to check.
346         * @return value, never null.
347         * @throws PropertyMissingException if value is null.
348         */
349        static <T> T require(String key, @Nullable T value) {
350                if (value == null) {
351                        throw new PropertyMissingException("Value is required not null. property key='" + key + "'");
352                }
353                return value;
354        }
355
356        /**
357         * Adds a fallback key to try (without <code>{name}</code> interpolation) if none of
358         * the keys tried so far are found. Keys already added are tried first, in order; this
359         * one is tried last.
360         * @param fallbackKey additional key to try.
361         * @return a new LogProperty trying this key's keys followed by fallbackKey.
362         */
363        default LogProperty or(String fallbackKey) {
364                validateKey(fallbackKey);
365                return withKey(fallbackKey);
366        }
367
368        /**
369         * Adds a fallback key to try (with <code>{name}</code> interpolated to nameParam) if
370         * none of the keys tried so far are found.
371         * @param fallbackKey additional key to try, containing a <code>{name}</code>
372         * placeholder.
373         * @param nameParam value to interpolate for <code>{name}</code>.
374         * @return a new LogProperty trying this key's keys followed by fallbackKey.
375         */
376        default LogProperty or(String fallbackKey, String nameParam) {
377                String interpolated = LogProperties.interpolateNamedKey(fallbackKey, nameParam);
378                validateKey(interpolated);
379                return withKey(interpolated);
380        }
381
382        private LogProperty withKey(String fallbackKey) {
383                List<String> combined = new ArrayList<>(keys());
384                combined.add(fallbackKey);
385                boolean sensitive = this instanceof DefaultLogProperty d && d.sensitive;
386                return new DefaultLogProperty(List.copyOf(combined), properties(), sensitive);
387        }
388
389        /**
390         * Marks the value as a secret, such as authentication headers. It is redacted in
391         * error messages and in the read properties report, and a value from the query of a
392         * component's URI is an error, since URIs end up in reports and error messages.
393         * Generated builders use this for parameters marked
394         * {@code LogConfigurable.SensitiveParameter}.
395         * @return a property with the same keys that treats its value as a secret.
396         * @apiNote Sensitive conversion failures retain the converter's exception type name
397         * and stack frames, but omit its original message, causes and suppressed exceptions,
398         * which may contain the value.
399         */
400        default LogProperty sensitive() {
401                return new DefaultLogProperty(keys(), properties(), true);
402        }
403
404        /**
405         * Creates a LogProperty for a single key.
406         * @param properties properties this key will be looked up against.
407         * @param key key.
408         * @return LogProperty.
409         */
410        static LogProperty of(LogProperties properties, String key) {
411                validateKey(key);
412                return new DefaultLogProperty(List.of(key), properties);
413        }
414
415        /**
416         * Creates a LogProperty for a single key with a <code>{name}</code> parameter
417         * interpolated.
418         * @param properties properties this key will be looked up against.
419         * @param key key, containing a <code>{name}</code> placeholder.
420         * @param nameParam value to interpolate for <code>{name}</code>.
421         * @return LogProperty.
422         */
423        static LogProperty of(LogProperties properties, String key, String nameParam) {
424                String interpolated = LogProperties.interpolateNamedKey(key, nameParam);
425                validateKey(interpolated);
426                return new DefaultLogProperty(List.of(interpolated), properties);
427        }
428
429        /**
430         * Validates a fully resolved (post <code>{name}</code> interpolation) property key -
431         * must start with {@value LogProperties#ROOT_PREFIX}, must not start or end with
432         * {@value LogProperties#SEP}, and must not use a reserved key parameter name.
433         * @param key fully resolved key to validate.
434         * @throws IllegalArgumentException if key is malformed.
435         */
436        private static void validateKey(String key) {
437                if (!key.startsWith(LogProperties.ROOT_PREFIX)) {
438                        throw new IllegalArgumentException(
439                                        "Property key should start with: '" + LogProperties.ROOT_PREFIX + "'. key = " + key);
440                }
441                if (key.endsWith(LogProperties.SEP) || key.startsWith(LogProperties.SEP)) {
442                        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Property key should not start or end with '" + LogProperties.SEP + "'");
443                }
444                LogProperties.validateKeyParameters(key, Set.of());
445        }
446
447        /**
448         * An error friendly {@link Function} for converting properties.
449         *
450         * @param <T> input type.
451         * @param <R> output type.
452         * @param <E> error type.
453         */
454        public interface PropertyFunction<T extends @Nullable Object, R extends @Nullable Object, E extends Exception>
455                        extends Function<T, R> {
456
457                @Override
458                default R apply(T t) {
459                        try {
460                                return _apply(t);
461                        }
462                        catch (Exception e) {
463                                sneakyThrow(e);
464                                throw new RuntimeException(e);
465                        }
466                }
467
468                /**
469                 * Apply that throws error.
470                 * @param t input
471                 * @return output
472                 * @throws E if an error happened in function.
473                 */
474                public R _apply(T t) throws E;
475
476                @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
477                private static <E extends Throwable> void sneakyThrow(final Throwable x) throws E {
478                        throw (E) x;
479                }
480
481        }
482
483        /**
484         * Parent interface for property exceptions.
485         */
486        sealed interface PropertyProblem permits PropertyConvertException, PropertyMissingException, ValidationException,
487                        LogProviderRef.NotFoundException {
488
489                /**
490                 * A short, stable name for this problem used in error messages instead of the
491                 * exception's full (and for a nested class, {@code $}-separated) class name.
492                 * Deliberately hardcoded per implementation rather than derived via
493                 * {@code getClass().getSimpleName()} so it stays stable across renames/moves of
494                 * the actual exception class.
495                 * @return error name.
496                 */
497                String errorName();
498
499        }
500
501        /**
502         * Property helper mixin.
503         */
504        interface PropertySupport {
505
506                /**
507                 * String key value properties.
508                 * @return properties.
509                 */
510                public LogProperties properties();
511
512        }
513
514        /**
515         * Thrown if an error happens while converting a property.
516         */
517        final static class PropertyConvertException extends RuntimeException implements PropertyProblem {
518
519                private static final long serialVersionUID = -6260241455268426342L;
520
521                /**
522                 * Key.
523                 */
524                private final String key;
525
526                /**
527                 * Creates convert exception.
528                 * @param key property key.
529                 * @param message error message
530                 * @param cause maybe null.
531                 */
532                PropertyConvertException(String key, String message, @Nullable Throwable cause) {
533                        super(message, cause);
534                        this.key = key;
535                }
536
537                /**
538                 * Property key.
539                 * @return key.
540                 */
541                public String key() {
542                        return this.key;
543                }
544
545                @Override
546                public String errorName() {
547                        return "PropertyConvertException";
548                }
549
550        }
551
552        /**
553         * Throw if property is missing.
554         */
555        final static class PropertyMissingException extends NoSuchElementException implements PropertyProblem {
556
557                private static final long serialVersionUID = 4203076848052565692L;
558
559                /**
560                 * Creates a missing property exception.
561                 * @param s error message.
562                 */
563                PropertyMissingException(String s) {
564                        super(s);
565                }
566
567                @Override
568                public String errorName() {
569                        return "PropertyMissingException";
570                }
571
572        }
573
574        /**
575         * Thrown by {@link Validator#validate()} when one or more of the accumulated
576         * {@link Result}s failed, reporting every failure in a single message instead of just
577         * the first one encountered.
578         */
579        final static class ValidationException extends RuntimeException implements PropertyProblem {
580
581                private static final long serialVersionUID = -8416817560218813225L;
582
583                ValidationException(String message, @Nullable Throwable cause) {
584                        super(message, cause);
585                }
586
587                @Override
588                public String errorName() {
589                        return "ValidationException";
590                }
591
592                /**
593                 * Validates a list of results and throws {@link ValidationException} if any
594                 * results are not {@link Result.Success}.
595                 * @param builder class to prefix to full message.
596                 * @param results list of results.
597                 * @throws ValidationException if any result in the supplied list is not
598                 * successful.
599                 */
600                public static void validate(Class<?> builder, List<Result<?>> results) throws ValidationException {
601                        StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder().append("Validation failed for ")
602                                .append(builder.getName())
603                                .append(":");
604                        Throwable cause = null;
605                        boolean failed = false;
606                        for (var r : results) {
607                                switch (r) {
608                                        case Result.Success<?> s -> {
609                                                continue;
610                                        }
611                                        case Result.Missing<?> m -> {
612                                                sb.append("\n");
613                                                sb.append(m.message());
614                                                failed = true;
615                                        }
616                                        case Result.Error<?> e -> {
617                                                sb.append("\n");
618                                                sb.append(e.message());
619                                                if (cause == null) {
620                                                        cause = e.cause();
621                                                }
622                                                failed = true;
623                                        }
624                                }
625                        }
626                        if (failed) {
627                                throw new ValidationException(sb.toString(), cause);
628                        }
629
630                }
631
632                /**
633                 * Wraps cause in a {@link ValidationException}, using the same "Validation failed
634                 * for &lt;class&gt;:" message prefix {@link #validate(Class, List)} itself uses.
635                 * {@link ValidationException}'s constructor is package-private, so this is the
636                 * supported way for code outside this package - generated builder code in
637                 * particular - to report a downstream factory method's own defensive/cross-field
638                 * check (an {@link IllegalArgumentException}, say) through the same channel as a
639                 * per-field validation failure, without duplicating the message format itself.
640                 * Returns rather than throws so the caller writes
641                 * {@code throw ValidationException.of(...)} - keeps the throw itself, and
642                 * therefore unreachable-code/definite-assignment analysis at the call site,
643                 * visible there instead of hidden inside this method.
644                 * @param builder class to prefix to the message, same role as
645                 * {@link #validate(Class, List)}'s own parameter.
646                 * @param cause the exception to wrap.
647                 * @return a new {@link ValidationException} wrapping cause; not thrown by this
648                 * method.
649                 */
650                public static ValidationException of(Class<?> builder, RuntimeException cause) {
651                        return new ValidationException("Validation failed for " + builder.getName() + ": " + cause.getMessage(),
652                                        cause);
653                }
654
655        }
656
657        /**
658         * Accumulates {@link Result}s from one or more property lookups and validates them
659         * together, so that a caller resolving several properties in sequence can report
660         * every failure at once instead of failing fast on the first bad property.
661         * <p>
662         * This is the mechanism generated {@code fromProperties(LogProperties)} builder
663         * implementations use: each property is looked up and its {@link Result} is added to
664         * the validator as it is read; {@link #validate()} is then called once at the end,
665         * after all properties have been read, so a user who misconfigured several properties
666         * sees all of the problems together rather than fixing them one at a time across
667         * repeated runs.
668         * <p>
669         * Use {@link #add(Result)} for a property that is required: a {@link Result.Missing}
670         * is treated as a failure. Use {@link #addIfError(Result)} for an optional property
671         * that already has a fallback applied (typically via {@link Result#or(Object)} with
672         * the builder's current field value): a {@link Result.Missing} is expected in that
673         * case and is silently ignored, but a {@link Result.Error} (the property was present
674         * but failed to convert) is still a real problem and is reported.
675         *
676         * @apiNote a {@code Validator} is single-use: create one with {@link #of(Class)}, add
677         * every result that should be checked, and call {@link #validate()} exactly once at
678         * the end.
679         */
680        public static class Validator {
681
682                private final List<Result<?>> results = new ArrayList<>();
683
684                private final Class<?> builder;
685
686                /**
687                 * Creates a validator whose {@link ValidationException} messages will be prefixed
688                 * with the name of the given class.
689                 * @param builder the class on whose behalf properties are being resolved -
690                 * typically the builder calling this method. It is only used to identify the
691                 * source of a failure in the exception message; no state is read from it.
692                 * @return newly created validator.
693                 */
694                public static Validator of(Class<?> builder) {
695                        return new Validator(builder);
696                }
697
698                private Validator(Class<?> builder) {
699                        this.builder = builder;
700                }
701
702                /**
703                 * Adds a result that must be present. Both {@link Result.Missing} and
704                 * {@link Result.Error} will cause {@link #validate()} to fail. Use this for a
705                 * required property; for an optional property that already has a fallback value
706                 * applied, use {@link #addIfError(Result)} instead so a missing value does not
707                 * itself trigger a failure.
708                 * @param result result to check.
709                 * @return this.
710                 */
711                public Validator add(Result<?> result) {
712                        results.add(result);
713                        return this;
714                }
715
716                /**
717                 * Adds a result only if it is a {@link Result.Error}; a {@link Result.Missing}
718                 * result is silently ignored. Intended for an optional property that has already
719                 * had a fallback value applied (for example via {@link Result#or(Object)}): the
720                 * property being absent is expected and fine, but if it was present and failed to
721                 * convert that should not be swallowed.
722                 * @param result result to check.
723                 * @return this.
724                 */
725                public Validator addIfError(Result<?> result) {
726                        if (result instanceof Result.Error<?> e) {
727                                results.add(e);
728                        }
729                        return this;
730                }
731
732                /**
733                 * Validates every result added so far via {@link #add(Result)} or
734                 * {@link #addIfError(Result)}, throwing a single exception listing all failures
735                 * if one or more of them are not {@link Result.Success}.
736                 * @throws ValidationException if any added result is a {@link Result.Missing}
737                 * (added via {@link #add(Result)}) or a {@link Result.Error} (added via either
738                 * method).
739                 */
740                public void validate() throws ValidationException {
741                        ValidationException.validate(builder, results);
742                }
743
744                /**
745                 * Validates every name in a list resolved from a comma-separated list property
746                 * (e.g. appenders/routes) before any of those names are used to construct
747                 * anything, so a bad name is reported against the list property itself rather
748                 * than against whatever unrelated {@code {name}}-keyed property a downstream
749                 * lookup happens to interpolate first. Static (rather than an instance method
750                 * using an existing {@link Validator}'s own {@code builder} field) since this
751                 * check is independent of - and never participates in - whatever else a
752                 * particular {@link Validator} instance may have accumulated via
753                 * {@link #add(Result)}/{@link #addIfError(Result)}.
754                 * @param component the class on whose behalf these names are being resolved -
755                 * used to prefix the thrown {@link ValidationException}'s message, the same role
756                 * {@link #of(Class)} plays elsewhere.
757                 * @param kind short noun describing what these names are (e.g.
758                 * {@code "appender"}, {@code "route"}), used only for the message.
759                 * @param source the result the list itself was resolved from, used only for its
760                 * {@link Result#describe()} in the message.
761                 * @param names names to validate.
762                 * @return names unchanged if all are valid.
763                 * @throws ValidationException if any name is blank or has other characters.
764                 */
765                static List<String> validateNames(Class<?> component, String kind, Result<?> source, List<String> names) {
766                        for (String name : names) {
767                                if (!isValidName(name)) {
768                                        throw ValidationException.of(component,
769                                                        new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid " + kind + " name '" + name + "' in "
770                                                                        + source.describe() + ": must be alphanumeric (hyphen/underscore allowed)"));
771                                }
772                        }
773                        return names;
774                }
775
776                /**
777                 * Validates that a key parameter token (the identifier inside <code>{...}</code>
778                 * in a key template, e.g. <code>"name"</code> in <code>a.{name}.b</code>) is well
779                 * formed: non-blank and made up only of letters, digits, <code>-</code>, or
780                 * <code>_</code>. This guards against a malformed key <em>template</em>, not user
781                 * input.
782                 * @param parameter parameter token found in a key template.
783                 * @return the parameter unchanged if valid.
784                 * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the parameter is blank or has other
785                 * characters.
786                 */
787                static String validateKeyParameter(String parameter) {
788                        if (!isValidName(parameter)) {
789                                throw new IllegalArgumentException(
790                                                "Key parameter must be alphanumeric (hyphen/underscore allowed). parameter: '" + parameter
791                                                                + "'");
792                        }
793                        return parameter;
794                }
795
796                /**
797                 * Validates that a value about to be interpolated for a <code>{name}</code>-style
798                 * key parameter is well formed: non-blank and made up only of letters, digits,
799                 * <code>-</code>, or <code>_</code>. This is the single choke point every
800                 * keyed-name mechanism in the project (appender/output/encoder/publisher/route
801                 * names, and every annotation-processor generated builder's own property prefix)
802                 * funnels through via {@link LogProperties#interpolateKey(String, Function)}.
803                 * @param key original, pre-interpolation key template (e.g.
804                 * <code>a.{name}.b</code>).
805                 * @param parameter name of the parameter being interpolated (e.g.
806                 * <code>"name"</code>).
807                 * @param value value about to be substituted for the parameter.
808                 * @return the value unchanged if valid.
809                 * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the value is blank or has other characters.
810                 */
811                static String validateKeyParameterValue(String key, String parameter, String value) {
812                        validateKeyParameter(parameter);
813                        if (!isValidName(value)) {
814                                throw new IllegalArgumentException("\"" + key + "\" cannot be interpolated: parameter '" + parameter
815                                                + "' value '" + value + "' must be alphanumeric (hyphen/underscore allowed)");
816                        }
817                        return value;
818                }
819
820                private static boolean isValidName(String s) {
821                        if (s.isBlank()) {
822                                return false;
823                        }
824                        for (int i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) {
825                                char c = s.charAt(i);
826                                if (!Character.isLetterOrDigit(c) && c != '-' && c != '_') {
827                                        return false;
828                                }
829                        }
830                        return true;
831                }
832
833        }
834
835        /**
836         * The result of a property fetched from properties.
837         *
838         * @param <T> property type.
839         */
840        sealed interface Result<T> {
841
842                /**
843                 * Registers this result with {@code validator} via {@link Validator#add(Result)}
844                 * (a still-{@link Missing} result is treated as a real failure) and returns this
845                 * result unchanged, so a chain that builds a required property can register
846                 * itself with a shared {@link Validator} and keep going in one expression -
847                 * {@code properties.forKey(key).ofString().or(fallback).validate(v)} - instead of
848                 * a separate {@code var x = ...; v.add(x);} statement pair. The validator is
849                 * shared and single-use by design: add every property's result this way (or via
850                 * {@link #validateIfError(Validator)} for an optional one), then call
851                 * {@link Validator#validate()} exactly once at the end to report every failure
852                 * together instead of one exception per property.
853                 * @param validator validator to add this result to.
854                 * @return this result, unchanged.
855                 */
856                default ValidatedResult<T> validate(Validator validator) {
857                        validator.add(this);
858                        return (ValidatedResult<T>) this;
859                }
860
861                /**
862                 * Like {@link #validate(Validator)} but via {@link Validator#addIfError(Result)}
863                 * instead of {@link Validator#add(Result)} - a {@link Missing} result is expected
864                 * and ignored, only a {@link Result.Error} is treated as a failure. Intended for
865                 * an optional property that already has a fallback applied (for example via
866                 * {@link #or(Object)}): the property being absent is fine, but if it was present
867                 * and failed to convert that should not be swallowed.
868                 * @param validator validator to add this result to.
869                 * @return this result, unchanged.
870                 */
871                default ValidatedResult<T> validateIfError(Validator validator) {
872                        validator.addIfError(this);
873                        return (ValidatedResult<T>) this;
874                }
875
876                /**
877                 * Convenience for a genuine one-off, single-property validation that does not
878                 * need to participate in a larger batch: builds a single-use {@link Validator},
879                 * registers this result with it via {@link Validator#add(Result)}, and validates
880                 * immediately - instead of registering with a caller-managed {@link Validator}
881                 * via {@link #validate(Validator)} and deferring to a later
882                 * {@link Validator#validate()} call.
883                 * <p>
884                 * Uses {@link Validator#add(Result)} semantics: a still-{@link Missing} result is
885                 * treated as a failure, same as an absent required property with no fallback. If
886                 * this property is optional, apply a fallback first -
887                 * {@code properties.forKey(key).ofString().or(fallback).validateNow(component)} -
888                 * since a result with a fallback applied is never {@link Missing}. For a property
889                 * that should tolerate being missing but not being present-and-malformed, use
890                 * {@link #validateIfError(Validator)} with an externally-owned {@link Validator}
891                 * instead - there is deliberately no addIfError-equivalent of this method, to
892                 * avoid two same-named single-property convenience methods with silently
893                 * different failure semantics.
894                 * @param component the class on whose behalf this property is being resolved -
895                 * only used to name the source of the failure in the exception message.
896                 * @return value.
897                 * @throws ValidationException if this result is not a {@link Success}.
898                 */
899                default T validateNow(Class<?> component) {
900                        var v = Validator.of(component);
901                        v.add(this);
902                        v.validate();
903                        var result = switch (this) {
904                                case ValidatedResult<T> vr -> vr;
905                        };
906                        return result.value();
907                }
908
909                /**
910                 * Returns the current result if fallback is null or returns fallback as a result
911                 * if this result is missing.
912                 * @param fallback maybe <code>null</code>.
913                 * @return value.
914                 */
915                public Result<T> or(@Nullable T fallback);
916
917                /**
918                 * Returns the current result if success or error otherwise fallback supplier is
919                 * used. If the supplier returns <code>null</code> then the result will be mising.
920                 * @param fallback may return <code>null</code> but not recommended.
921                 * @return value.
922                 */
923                public Result<T> or(Supplier<T> fallback);
924
925                /**
926                 * Maps this result's value through {@code mapper}. On success, keeps the origin
927                 * ({@link PropertySuccess#topProperties() topProperties}/properties/key/
928                 * rawValue/kind, see {@link PropertySuccess}) so a later conversion step's error
929                 * message can still point back to it. On failure, builds a rich error message -
930                 * which key it came from, where that key was found, and (for
931                 * {@link PropertyConvertException}/{@link ValidationException} causes) the
932                 * original raw value - with a "Tried:" line searching {@code topProperties}: the
933                 * {@link LogProperties} the very first {@link LogProperties#forKey(String)} in
934                 * this chain was looked up against, which for a chained/composite
935                 * {@code LogProperties.of(a, b)} can be broader than the exact source the value
936                 * was actually found at. Usable at any point in a chain, not just directly off a
937                 * {@link LogProperty}, since a {@link Success} keeps pointing back to the
938                 * property it originally came from no matter how many conversions have run since.
939                 * @param <U> result type
940                 * @param mapper mapping function.
941                 * @return mapped result.
942                 */
943                public <U> Result<U> map(PropertyFunction<T, U, ? super Exception> mapper);
944
945                /**
946                 * A description of the result for error messages.
947                 * @return description.
948                 */
949                public String describe();
950
951                /**
952                 * A property that is present.
953                 *
954                 * @param <T> property type.
955                 */
956                public sealed interface Success<T> extends RequiredResult<T> permits PropertySuccess {
957
958                        @Override
959                        default @Nullable T valueOrNull() {
960                                return value();
961                        }
962
963                        /**
964                         * Gets the value and will never fail for Success.
965                         * @return value.
966                         */
967                        @Override
968                        public T value();
969
970                        @Override
971                        default Success<T> or(@Nullable T fallback) {
972                                return this;
973                        }
974
975                        @Override
976                        default Success<T> or(Supplier<T> fallback) {
977                                return this;
978                        }
979
980                        /**
981                         * Original property key where the value was derived from or was passed a
982                         * fallback.
983                         * @return key.
984                         */
985                        public String key();
986
987                }
988
989                /**
990                 * A property that is missing (<code>null</code>).
991                 *
992                 * @param <T> property type.
993                 * @param properties the properties that were searched, kept around so
994                 * {@link #or(Object)} can hand it to the {@link PropertySuccess} it builds for a
995                 * supplied fallback.
996                 * @param keys keys.
997                 * @param message description of where the property is missing.
998                 * @param sensitive whether a supplied fallback must also be treated as a secret.
999                 */
1000                public record Missing<T>(LogProperties properties, List<String> keys, String message,
1001                                boolean sensitive) implements ValidatedResult<T> {
1002                        /**
1003                         * Creates a missing result for a property that is not marked sensitive.
1004                         * @param properties the properties that were searched.
1005                         * @param keys keys.
1006                         * @param message description of where the property is missing.
1007                         */
1008                        public Missing(LogProperties properties, List<String> keys, String message) {
1009                                this(properties, keys, message, false);
1010                        }
1011
1012                        /**
1013                         * A property that is missing (<code>null</code>).
1014                         * @param properties the properties that were searched.
1015                         * @param keys keys.
1016                         * @param message description of where the property is missing.
1017                         * @param sensitive whether a fallback is sensitive.
1018                         */
1019                        public Missing {
1020                                if (keys.isEmpty()) {
1021                                        throw new IllegalArgumentException("one key is required");
1022                                }
1023                        }
1024
1025                        @Override
1026                        public @Nullable T valueOrNull() {
1027                                return null;
1028                        }
1029
1030                        @Override
1031                        public T value() throws NoSuchElementException {
1032                                throw new PropertyMissingException(message);
1033                        }
1034
1035                        @Override
1036                        public Result<T> or(@Nullable T fallback) {
1037                                if (fallback != null) {
1038                                        return new PropertySuccess<>(properties, properties, keys.get(0), fallback,
1039                                                        PropertySuccess.Kind.VALUE, fallback, sensitive);
1040                                }
1041                                return this;
1042                        }
1043
1044                        @Override
1045                        public Result<T> or(Supplier<T> fallback) {
1046                                return or(fallback.get());
1047                        }
1048
1049                        /**
1050                         * Helper just to cast the result to a different parameterized type.
1051                         * @param <R> parameterized type.
1052                         * @return this.
1053                         */
1054                        @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
1055                        public <R> Missing<R> convert() {
1056                                return (Missing<R>) this;
1057                        }
1058
1059                        @Override
1060                        public <U> Missing<U> map(PropertyFunction<T, U, ? super Exception> mapper) {
1061                                return convert();
1062                        }
1063
1064                        @Override
1065                        public String describe() {
1066                                return "Missing[" + keys + "]";
1067                        }
1068
1069                }
1070
1071                /**
1072                 * A property that was present but failed conversion.
1073                 *
1074                 * @param <T> property type.
1075                 * @param key property key that failed to convert.
1076                 * @param message failure message.
1077                 * @param cause exception thrown while trying to convert.
1078                 */
1079                @SuppressWarnings("JavaLangClash")
1080                public record Error<T>(String key, String message, Exception cause) implements ValidatedResult<T> {
1081                        /*
1082                         * TODO consider rename to Failure
1083                         */
1084                        @Override
1085                        public @Nullable T valueOrNull() {
1086                                throw new PropertyConvertException(key, message, cause);
1087                        }
1088
1089                        @Override
1090                        public T value() throws PropertyConvertException {
1091                                throw new PropertyConvertException(key, message, cause);
1092                        }
1093
1094                        @Override
1095                        public Error<T> or(@Nullable T fallback) {
1096                                return this;
1097                        }
1098
1099                        @Override
1100                        public Error<T> or(Supplier<T> fallback) {
1101                                return this;
1102                        }
1103
1104                        /**
1105                         * Helper just to cast the result to a different parameterized type.
1106                         * @param <R> parameterized type.
1107                         * @return this.
1108                         */
1109                        @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
1110                        public <R> Error<R> convert() {
1111                                return (Error<R>) this;
1112                        }
1113
1114                        @Override
1115                        public <U> Error<U> map(PropertyFunction<T, U, ? super Exception> mapper) {
1116                                return convert();
1117                        }
1118
1119                        @Override
1120                        public String describe() {
1121                                return "Error[" + key + "](" + message + ")";
1122                        }
1123                }
1124
1125        }
1126
1127        /**
1128         * A {@link Result} that is safe to pull a value out of - either because it can never
1129         * actually be missing ({@link RequiredResult}: a {@link Success} or an
1130         * {@link Result.Error}, both already resolved one way or the other) or because a
1131         * caller has explicitly acknowledged the possibility of a still-{@link Missing}
1132         * result by running it through {@link Result#validate(Validator)},
1133         * {@link Result#validateIfError(Validator)}, or {@link Result#validateNow(Class)}.
1134         * <p>
1135         * {@link Result} itself deliberately does not declare {@link #value()}/
1136         * {@link #valueOrNull()}/{@link #optional()} - a bare {@link Result} returned by
1137         * {@link LogProperty#ofString()} and friends forces a caller through one of those
1138         * validation paths before it can pull a value out, instead of blindly calling
1139         * {@code value()} on a result that might still be {@link Missing}.
1140         *
1141         * @param <T> property type.
1142         */
1143        sealed interface ValidatedResult<T> extends Result<T> {
1144
1145                /**
1146                 * Gets the value and will fail with {@link NoSuchElementException} if there is no
1147                 * value.
1148                 * @return value.
1149                 * @throws PropertyMissingException if there is no value.
1150                 * @throws PropertyConvertException if the property failed conversion.
1151                 */
1152                public T value() throws PropertyMissingException, PropertyConvertException;
1153
1154                /**
1155                 * Gets the value.
1156                 * @return value or <code>null</code>.
1157                 */
1158                public @Nullable T valueOrNull();
1159
1160                /**
1161                 * Gets a value if there is if not uses the fallback.
1162                 * @param fallback maybe <code>null</code>.
1163                 * @return value.
1164                 */
1165                default @Nullable T valueOrNull(@Nullable T fallback) {
1166                        var v = valueOrNull();
1167                        if (v != null) {
1168                                return v;
1169                        }
1170                        return fallback;
1171                }
1172
1173                /**
1174                 * Convenience that turns a value into an optional.
1175                 * @return optional.
1176                 */
1177                default Optional<T> optional() {
1178                        return Optional.ofNullable(valueOrNull());
1179                }
1180
1181        }
1182
1183        /**
1184         * A result that is not missing and will either be an error or success.
1185         *
1186         * @param <T> property type.
1187         */
1188        sealed interface RequiredResult<T> extends ValidatedResult<T> {
1189
1190        }
1191
1192}
1193
1194/**
1195 * A property that is present, either because it was actually found in properties, or
1196 * (when {@code kind} is {@link Kind#VALUE}) because it was missing there and a fallback
1197 * value was supplied instead.
1198 * <p>
1199 * Not public: nothing outside {@code LogProperty}'s own resolution machinery (in this
1200 * package) constructs or pattern-matches on this directly - callers work through the
1201 * sealed {@link LogProperty.Result}/{@link LogProperty.Result.Success} interfaces
1202 * instead.
1203 *
1204 * @param <T> property type.
1205 * @param topProperties the {@link LogProperties} the very first
1206 * {@link LogProperties#forKey(String)} in this chain was looked up against - for a
1207 * chained/composite {@code LogProperties.of(a, b)} this is the whole composite, not just
1208 * whichever member the value ended up found in. Used for a failure message's "Tried:"
1209 * line, which can therefore search more broadly than {@code properties}.
1210 * @param properties the properties searched; for {@link Kind#STRING}/{@link Kind#LIST}/
1211 * {@link Kind#MAP} the <strong>exact</strong> properties where the value was found - for
1212 * a chained/composite search this can be narrower than {@code topProperties}, naming just
1213 * the one member the value was actually found in. Used for a failure message's "key: ...
1214 * from X" line.
1215 * @param key property key.
1216 * @param rawValue value as originally found (or the fallback, for {@link Kind#VALUE}),
1217 * before any conversion - a {@link String}, {@link List List&lt;String&gt;}, or
1218 * {@link Map Map&lt;String,String&gt;} depending on kind.
1219 * @param kind which of {@link LogProperty}'s {@code ofString()}/{@code ofList()}/
1220 * {@code ofMap()} this property was found through, and so rawValue's runtime type - or
1221 * {@link Kind#VALUE} if it was not found at all and rawValue is a fallback.
1222 * @param value actual (possibly converted) value.
1223 * @apiNote rawValue/kind stick around after a conversion (e.g.
1224 * {@link LogProperty#ofInt()} converting the string this was found as into an
1225 * {@code Integer}) so error messages can still describe the original value - value's type
1226 * and rawValue's kind are not always in sync.
1227 */
1228record PropertySuccess<T>(LogProperties topProperties, LogProperties properties, String key, Object rawValue,
1229                PropertySuccess.Kind kind, T value, boolean sensitive) implements LogProperty.Result.Success<T> {
1230
1231        PropertySuccess(LogProperties topProperties, LogProperties properties, String key, Object rawValue,
1232                        PropertySuccess.Kind kind, T value) {
1233                this(topProperties, properties, key, rawValue, kind, value, false);
1234        }
1235
1236        /**
1237         * Which of {@link LogProperty}'s typed accessors a {@link PropertySuccess} was found
1238         * through, and so what {@link PropertySuccess#rawValue()}'s runtime type actually is
1239         * - or that it was not found at all and is a plain fallback value.
1240         */
1241        enum Kind {
1242
1243                /**
1244                 * rawValue is a {@link String}, found via {@link LogProperty#ofString()}.
1245                 */
1246                STRING,
1247                /**
1248                 * rawValue is a {@link List List&lt;String&gt;}, found via
1249                 * {@link LogProperty#ofList()}.
1250                 */
1251                LIST,
1252                /**
1253                 * rawValue is a {@link Map Map&lt;String,String&gt;}, found via
1254                 * {@link LogProperty#ofMap()}.
1255                 */
1256                MAP,
1257                /**
1258                 * Not found in properties at all - rawValue is a plain fallback value supplied
1259                 * via {@link LogProperty.Result#or}.
1260                 */
1261                VALUE
1262
1263        }
1264
1265        /**
1266         * Successfully found property value.
1267         * @param topProperties the properties the original lookup started from.
1268         * @param properties the properties searched.
1269         * @param key property key.
1270         * @param rawValue value as originally found (or the fallback), before any conversion.
1271         * @param kind rawValue's kind.
1272         * @param value actual value should not be <code>null</code>.
1273         * @param sensitive whether the value is a secret that is never shown.
1274         */
1275        PropertySuccess {
1276                if (value == null) {
1277                        throw new NullPointerException("value");
1278                }
1279        }
1280
1281        @Override
1282        public <U> LogProperty.Result<U> map(LogProperty.PropertyFunction<T, U, ? super Exception> mapper) {
1283                try {
1284                        U u = mapper._apply(value);
1285                        return new PropertySuccess<>(topProperties, properties, key, rawValue, kind, u, sensitive);
1286                }
1287                catch (Exception e) {
1288                        return LogProperty.richError(this, e);
1289                }
1290        }
1291
1292        @Override
1293        public String describe() {
1294                if (kind == Kind.VALUE) {
1295                        return "Fallback[" + key + "]="
1296                                        + (sensitive ? LogRedactor.REDACTED_VALUE : LogRedactor.redactProperty(key, String.valueOf(value)));
1297                }
1298                return "Property[" + key + "]=" + valueDescription();
1299        }
1300
1301        @Override
1302        public String toString() {
1303                return describe();
1304        }
1305
1306        String valueDescription() {
1307                if (sensitive) {
1308                        return LogRedactor.REDACTED_VALUE;
1309                }
1310                String s = kind == Kind.STRING ? (String) rawValue : String.valueOf(rawValue);
1311                return LogRedactor.redactProperty(key, s);
1312        }
1313
1314        PropertySuccess<T> asSensitive() {
1315                return new PropertySuccess<>(topProperties, properties, key, rawValue, kind, value, true);
1316        }
1317
1318}
1319
1320final class LogRedactor {
1321
1322        private LogRedactor() {
1323        }
1324
1325        private static final Set<String> REDACTED_KEYS = Set.of("password", "apikey", "secret", "token", "passwd",
1326                        "passphrase", "credential", "privatekey", "accesskey", "authorization");
1327
1328        static final String REDACTED_VALUE = "<REDACTED>";
1329
1330        /*
1331         * Keep the converter's type and frames for debugging, but no original throwable: its
1332         * message, cause or suppressed exceptions can each contain the secret.
1333         */
1334        static IllegalArgumentException redactException(Exception exception) {
1335                var safe = new IllegalArgumentException(
1336                                exception.getClass().getName() + ": the value is not shown because it is sensitive");
1337                safe.setStackTrace(exception.getStackTrace());
1338                return safe;
1339        }
1340
1341        static String redactProperty(String key, String input) {
1342                if (sensitiveKey(key)) {
1343                        return REDACTED_VALUE;
1344                }
1345                if (input.indexOf('?') < 0 && input.indexOf('@') < 0) {
1346                        return input;
1347                }
1348                try {
1349                        return redactUri(new URI(input));
1350                }
1351                catch (URISyntaxException e) {
1352                        return input;
1353                }
1354        }
1355
1356        /*
1357         * For listing values rather than describing one in an error: a value that is not a
1358         * URI can still hold sensitive pairs, such as a map property written as
1359         * Authorization=Bearer x.
1360         */
1361        static String redactValue(String key, String value) {
1362                String redacted = redactProperty(key, value);
1363                return redacted.indexOf('=') < 0 ? redacted : redactQuery(redacted);
1364        }
1365
1366        private static boolean sensitiveKey(String key) {
1367                String normalizedKey = key.toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT).replace(".", "").replace("_", "").replace("-", "");
1368                for (var k : REDACTED_KEYS) {
1369                        if (normalizedKey.contains(k)) {
1370                                return true;
1371                        }
1372                }
1373                return false;
1374        }
1375
1376        static String redactUri(URI uri) {
1377                String source = uri.toString();
1378                var result = new StringBuilder(source);
1379                String query = uri.getRawQuery();
1380                if (query != null) {
1381                        int queryStart = source.indexOf('?') + 1;
1382                        result.replace(queryStart, queryStart + query.length(), redactQuery(query, true));
1383                }
1384                String authority = uri.getRawAuthority();
1385                if (authority != null) {
1386                        int userInfoEnd = authority.lastIndexOf('@');
1387                        if (userInfoEnd >= 0) {
1388                                String scheme = uri.getScheme();
1389                                int authorityStart = scheme == null ? 2 : scheme.length() + 3;
1390                                result.replace(authorityStart, authorityStart + userInfoEnd, REDACTED_VALUE);
1391                        }
1392                }
1393                return result.toString();
1394        }
1395
1396        /*
1397         * A value can itself be a URI with user information or a map with sensitive keys.
1398         * Redact the whole value so neither the parent URI nor its source description can
1399         * expose credentials that are masked when the decoded property is shown on its own.
1400         */
1401        private static boolean sensitiveValue(String value) {
1402                String decoded = PercentCodec.decode(value, StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
1403                if (decoded.indexOf('@') >= 0) {
1404                        try {
1405                                String authority = new URI(decoded).getRawAuthority();
1406                                if (authority != null && authority.lastIndexOf('@') >= 0) {
1407                                        return true;
1408                                }
1409                        }
1410                        catch (URISyntaxException e) {
1411                                // A map value need not be a valid URI; check its keys below.
1412                        }
1413                }
1414                return decoded.indexOf('=') >= 0 && !redactQuery(decoded).equals(decoded);
1415        }
1416
1417        private static String redactQuery(String query) {
1418                return redactQuery(query, false);
1419        }
1420
1421        private static String redactQuery(String query, boolean allValues) {
1422                var result = new StringBuilder();
1423                int start = 0;
1424                for (int i = 0; i <= query.length(); i++) {
1425                        if (i == query.length() || query.charAt(i) == '&' || query.charAt(i) == ',') {
1426                                String pair = query.substring(start, i);
1427                                int equals = pair.indexOf('=');
1428                                if (equals >= 0) {
1429                                        String key = pair.substring(0, equals);
1430                                        String value = pair.substring(equals + 1);
1431                                        String decodedKey = PercentCodec.decode(key, StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
1432                                        result.append(key)
1433                                                .append('=')
1434                                                .append(allValues || sensitiveKey(decodedKey) || sensitiveValue(value) ? REDACTED_VALUE
1435                                                                : value);
1436                                }
1437                                else {
1438                                        result.append(pair);
1439                                }
1440                                if (i < query.length()) {
1441                                        result.append(query.charAt(i));
1442                                }
1443                                start = i + 1;
1444                        }
1445                }
1446                return result.toString();
1447        }
1448
1449}
1450
1451final class DefaultLogProperty implements LogProperty {
1452
1453        private final List<String> keys;
1454
1455        private final LogProperties properties;
1456
1457        final boolean sensitive;
1458
1459        DefaultLogProperty(List<String> keys, LogProperties properties) {
1460                this(keys, properties, false);
1461        }
1462
1463        DefaultLogProperty(List<String> keys, LogProperties properties, boolean sensitive) {
1464                super();
1465                if (keys.isEmpty()) {
1466                        throw new IllegalArgumentException("at least one key is required");
1467                }
1468                this.keys = keys;
1469                this.properties = properties;
1470                this.sensitive = sensitive;
1471        }
1472
1473        /*
1474         * A key built from a logger name. A facade can pass any string as a logger name, so
1475         * unlike a key in code it is not validated: a name like Testcontainers'
1476         * "tc.image@sha256:405c128b..." must fall back to its parents instead of throwing.
1477         * The root logger is also read from its alias.
1478         */
1479        static LogProperty ofLoggerKey(LogProperties properties, String prefix, String loggerName) {
1480                if (loggerName.isEmpty()) {
1481                        return new DefaultLogProperty(List.of(prefix), new Loggers.RootProperties(properties));
1482                }
1483                return new DefaultLogProperty(List.of(Loggers.Key.key(prefix, loggerName)), properties);
1484        }
1485
1486        @Override
1487        public String key() {
1488                return keys.get(0);
1489        }
1490
1491        @Override
1492        public List<String> keys() {
1493                return keys;
1494        }
1495
1496        @Override
1497        public LogProperties properties() {
1498                return this.properties;
1499        }
1500
1501        @Override
1502        public Result<String> ofString() {
1503                return resolve(k -> properties.visit(k, (p, kk) -> {
1504                        var v = p.valueOrNull(kk);
1505                        return v == null ? null : new PropertySuccess<>(properties, p, kk, v, PropertySuccess.Kind.STRING, v);
1506                }));
1507        }
1508
1509        @Override
1510        public Result<List<String>> ofList() {
1511                return resolve(k -> properties.visit(k, (p, kk) -> {
1512                        var v = p.listOrNull(kk);
1513                        return v == null ? null : new PropertySuccess<>(properties, p, kk, v, PropertySuccess.Kind.LIST, v);
1514                }));
1515        }
1516
1517        @Override
1518        public Result<Map<String, String>> ofMap() {
1519                try {
1520                        return resolve(k -> properties.visit(k, (p, kk) -> {
1521                                Map<String, String> v;
1522                                try {
1523                                        v = p.mapOrNull(kk);
1524                                }
1525                                catch (IllegalArgumentException e) {
1526                                        throw new MapFormException("'" + kk + "' from " + p.description(kk), e);
1527                                }
1528                                return v == null ? null : new PropertySuccess<>(properties, p, kk, v, PropertySuccess.Kind.MAP, v);
1529                        }));
1530                }
1531                catch (MapFormException e) {
1532                        var cause = sensitive ? LogRedactor.redactException(e.cause) : e.cause;
1533                        return new Result.Error<>(e.resolvedKey,
1534                                        "Error for property. key: " + e.resolvedKey + ", " + cause.getMessage(), cause);
1535                }
1536        }
1537
1538        /*
1539         * Carries which source rejected a map's form out of the visit, so the error names the
1540         * key and source the way every other property error does.
1541         */
1542        @SuppressWarnings("serial")
1543        private static final class MapFormException extends RuntimeException {
1544
1545                final String resolvedKey;
1546
1547                final IllegalArgumentException cause;
1548
1549                MapFormException(String resolvedKey, IllegalArgumentException cause) {
1550                        super(null, cause, false, false);
1551                        this.resolvedKey = resolvedKey;
1552                        this.cause = cause;
1553                }
1554
1555        }
1556
1557        private <T> Result<T> resolve(java.util.function.Function<String, Result.@Nullable Success<T>> lookup) {
1558                if (sensitive) {
1559                        var check = UnusedKeyCheck.findOrNull(properties);
1560                        if (check != null) {
1561                                for (String k : keys) {
1562                                        check.sensitive(k);
1563                                }
1564                        }
1565                        for (String k : keys) {
1566                                Result.@Nullable Error<T> error = uriQueryErrorOrNull(k);
1567                                if (error != null) {
1568                                        return error;
1569                                }
1570                        }
1571                }
1572                for (String k : keys) {
1573                        var success = lookup.apply(k);
1574                        if (success != null) {
1575                                return sensitive ? sensitive(success) : success;
1576                        }
1577                }
1578                return missingResult(properties, keys);
1579        }
1580
1581        /*
1582         * A URI is shown in reports and error messages, so a secret is refused there rather
1583         * than trusted to be redacted, even when a property overrides it. The message names
1584         * the keys, never the URI.
1585         */
1586        private <T> Result.@Nullable Error<T> uriQueryErrorOrNull(String key) {
1587                var uri = properties.<@Nullable UriQueryProperties>visit(key,
1588                                (p, k) -> p instanceof UriQueryProperties u && u.sets(k) ? u : null);
1589                if (uri == null) {
1590                        return null;
1591                }
1592                String uriKey = uri.uriKey();
1593                String from = uriKey == null ? "a component's URI" : "the URI of '" + uriKey + "'";
1594                String message = "Error for property. key: '" + key + "' is sensitive, so it cannot be set in the query of "
1595                                + from + ". Set '" + key + "' as its own property instead.";
1596                return new Result.Error<>(key, message, new IllegalArgumentException(message));
1597        }
1598
1599        private <T> Result<T> sensitive(Result.Success<T> success) {
1600                PropertySuccess<T> ps = switch (success) {
1601                        case PropertySuccess<T> p -> p;
1602                };
1603                return ps.asSensitive();
1604        }
1605
1606        <T> Result.Missing<T> missingResult(LogProperties props, List<String> keys) {
1607                List<String> resolvedKeys = describeKeys(props, keys);
1608                String label = keys.size() == 1 ? "key" : "keys";
1609                String message = "Property missing. " + label + ": " + resolvedKeys;
1610                if (message.length() > 120) {
1611                        var descriptions = new ArrayList<String>();
1612                        for (var key : keys) {
1613                                String fqk = fullyQualifiedKey(key);
1614                                var sources = new ArrayList<String>();
1615                                props.visit(fqk, (source, sourceKey) -> {
1616                                        sources.add(source.description(sourceKey));
1617                                        return null;
1618                                });
1619                                descriptions.add("'" + fqk + "' from:\n        " + String.join(",\n        ", sources));
1620                        }
1621                        message = "Property missing. " + label + ":\n    " + String.join(",\n    ", descriptions);
1622                }
1623                return new Result.Missing<>(props, keys, message, sensitive);
1624        }
1625
1626        List<String> describeKeys(LogProperties props, List<String> keys) {
1627                return keys.stream().<String>map(k -> {
1628                        String fqk = fullyQualifiedKey(k);
1629                        return "'" + fqk + "' from " + props.description(fullyQualifiedKey(k));
1630                }).toList();
1631        }
1632
1633        String fullyQualifiedKey(String key) {
1634                return key;
1635        }
1636
1637}
